profile.campus: Sterling, Loudoun County, Virginia (CyrusOne Northern Virginia campus, NVA7)
profile.reading:
Per CyrusOne's own official facility page, this NVA7 building (or campus) sits at 21350 Pacific Boulevard, Sterling, VA 20166 and publishes  of technical space and 116 MW of total IT capacity across the shared NVA5-NVA7 campus (not confirmed as this single building's individual figure) of technical space and 116 MW of total IT capacity across the shared NVA5-NVA7 campus. 

This facility is part of CyrusOne's broader Sterling, Virginia data center campus in Loudoun County, part of the Northern Virginia Ashburn-area data center corridor described by industry press as the world's densest concentration of data center capacity. Wikipedia's entry on CyrusOne states the company purchased 40 acres in Loudoun County in June 2016 for data center construction; CyrusOne itself was founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten, was headquartered in Dallas, Texas, went public in 2013, and was taken private in November 2021/2022 when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts (KKR) and Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) acquired the company in a deal valued at approximately $15 billion; the acquisition closed in March 2022 and CyrusOne is no longer an SEC filer for current-period results. The Sterling campus sits alongside separate NVA-numbered buildings tracked elsewhere in this registry (NVA1 through NVA9), reflecting a data center operator practice, also seen at Digital Realty, Equinix and QTS in this same corridor, of numbering sequential buildings on a shared or adjacent multi-parcel campus rather than giving each building an entirely distinct site name.

Loudoun County's Board of Supervisors has repeatedly cited data center real estate and business-license tax revenue as a major share of the county's budget, while Dominion Energy, the region's dominant electric utility, has flagged data center demand growth in Northern Virginia as a primary driver of its own long-term transmission and generation planning; CyrusOne's Sterling campus draws power from this same regional grid alongside neighboring hyperscale and colocation buildings operated by Amazon, Equinix, Digital Realty, and QTS in the same Ashburn-Sterling-Loudoun County corridor.

reading.body:
CyrusOne NVA7 is part of a three-building Sterling campus in Loudoun County, Virginia that publishes 116 MW of total IT capacity across NVA5, NVA6, and NVA7 combined. The individual building figures are not separated in published specifications, so the 116 MW cannot be confirmed as this single facility's capacity. At a nominal 40 kW per rack typical of AI training density, 116 MW across the entire campus would support roughly 2,900 racks, assuming even distribution across the three buildings. The campus occupies 1.18 million square feet in Sterling.

This campus sits in the Ashburn-Sterling-Loudoun County corridor, which industry sources describe as the world's densest data center concentration. Virginia publishes capacity figures from 25 of its 330 mapped data center facilities, totaling 1,603 MW. The NVA5-NVA7 campus ranks 26th in the state by published megawattage, well below the largest regional operators but within the published tier. CyrusOne is now privately held after a 2022 take-private by KKR and Global Infrastructure Partners.

Power for the Sterling campus comes from Dominion Energy's regional grid, which the utility has identified as facing sustained demand pressure from Northern Virginia data center growth. CyrusOne's Loudoun County holdings, acquired in 2016, share the same utility infrastructure and regional transmission constraints as neighboring hyperscale and colocation facilities operated by Amazon, Equinix, Digital Realty, and QTS in the same corridor. The facility's significance to AI scaling depends on whether the operator's total Northern Virginia capacity and grid headroom can absorb future tenant demand, facts not published at the building level.
